_note: The Story of Prophet al-Yasaʿ (Elisha), drawn strictly from the Qur'an (Surahs al-An'am and Sad). The Qur'an honours al-Yasaʿ twice — naming him among the prophets preferred above the worlds and among the outstanding — but relates no narrative of his life; by tradition he was the companion and successor of Ilyas among the Children of Israel. This chronicle says only what the text says. No figural imagery; summaries carry no Arabic script.

places.name: The Land of the Children of Israel

events.title: Among Those Preferred
events.summary: 'And Ismail and al-Yasaʿ and Yunus and Lut — and all We preferred over the worlds.' The Qur'an names al-Yasaʿ within a list of prophets whom Allah favoured above all peoples, granting him a place in the chain of guidance though it tells no story of his deeds.
events.why: The honour of al-Yasaʿ is precisely that Allah names him and prefers him. Where the Qur'an is silent on the details, it is enough for the believer to know he was chosen — and to leave the rest unclaimed.

media.caption: Calligraphic panel — “All We preferred over the worlds” (al-An'am 6:86).

events.title: Among the Outstanding
events.summary: 'And remember Ismail, al-Yasaʿ, and Dhul-Kifl, and all are among the outstanding.' The Qur'an gathers al-Yasaʿ a second time with the chosen, sealing his rank among the best of the servants of Allah — again without recounting a single event of his life.
events.why: Twice named, twice praised, and never narrated: al-Yasaʿ teaches the reader the discipline of the Qur'an itself — to honour whom Allah honours, and to invent nothing where He has left the page bare.

media.caption: Calligraphic panel — “All are among the outstanding” (Sad 38:48).

paths.title: The Arc of al-Yasaʿ
paths.blurb: All the Qur'an says of al-Yasaʿ — twice named among the chosen: preferred above the worlds, and counted among the outstanding.
